extracted.intended_audience: journalists, local news leaders, media researchers, funders, and policymakers interested in public trust in local news
extracted.subtask_description: A survey-based evaluation framework for assessing public trust and performance of local news organizations across roles, coverage topics, presentation quality, perceived bias, and audience engagement. Uses Gallup panel data to report levels, partisan and demographic differences, and drivers of trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall trust in reporting by local news organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you trust reporting by local news organizations 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' (vs. national news)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key headline metric (45% high trust for local vs. 31% for national). Survey uses a five-point scale (a great deal, quite a lot, some, very little, none); many respondents choose the middle 'some' option, indicating tepid support. Compare across parties, age, race, and attention to news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing factual local news reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Do news organizations in your local area do an excellent/good/fair/poor job providing factual local news reports?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the job-performance dimensions with partisan gaps (75% of Democrats rate excellent/good vs. 54% of Republicans). Tracked as % 'excellent' or 'good.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting people or groups that make a difference in your local area
rubrics_metrics.description: Do local news organizations do an excellent/good/fair/poor job highlighting people or groups that make a difference in your local area?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as part of job-performance battery; majority positive but varies by attention and community attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educating people about what is going on in their local area
rubrics_metrics.description: Do local news organizations do an excellent/good/fair/poor job educating people about what is going on in their local area?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority report 'excellent' or 'good' (61% across sample). Strongly correlated with attention to local news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making sure people have the knowledge to be informed about public affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Do local news organizations do an excellent/good/fair/poor job making sure people in your local area have the knowledge they need to be informed about public affairs?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of core civic function measures; used to assess democratic role performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making people feel inspired or uplifted by others in the local area
rubrics_metrics.description: Do local news organizations do an excellent/good/fair/poor job making people feel inspired or uplifted by others in the local area?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the weaker performance areas (52% rate only fair/poor). Included to capture community-building role rather than watchdog/reporting roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding local leaders accountable for their actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do local news organizations do an excellent/good/fair/poor job holding local leaders in politics, business and other institutions accountable for their actions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted deficiency: 60% say only fair/poor. Considered a key democratic responsibility; low ratings indicate perceived weakness in accountability reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Weather
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover weather (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of 14 topic-specific coverage metrics; weather ranked highest (77% excellent/good). Dissatisfaction often tied to quality rather than amount for weather coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Local sports teams
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover local sports teams (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High approval (69% excellent/good); used as part of topic-by-topic performance assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Local entertainment, arts, culture and events
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover local entertainment, arts, culture and events (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured among 14 topics; relatively strong performance; dissatisfaction patterns (amount vs. quality) vary by topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Crime and public safety
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover crime and public safety (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority positive but many dissatisfied respondents cite quality problems rather than insufficient attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Traffic and public transportation
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover traffic and public transportation (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among routine local service topics; approval higher among those attentive to local news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Local lifestyle topics (health, food, exercise, parenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover lifestyle topics such as health, food, exercise or parenting (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured to capture utility/interest content; approval varies with audience attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Plans for public works projects or business development
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover plans for public works projects or business development in your local area (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topic linked to local government and development coverage; dissatisfaction can signal gaps in accountability or depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Your local economy and business climate
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover your local economy and business climate (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of topical battery; approval linked to perceived relevance and utility of local reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Your local government and politics
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover your local government and politics (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower approval relative to nonpolitical topics; dissatisfaction often tied to perceived poor quality and weak accountability reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of The local real estate and housing market
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover the local real estate and housing market (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured because of public interest and policy relevance (61% say more coverage needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of K-12 education in your local area
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover K-12 education in your local area (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as an area needing more attention (64% want more coverage); dissatisfaction often about insufficient attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of The local environment and pollution
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover the local environment and pollution (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low approval (majority 'fair' or 'poor' for environment); many dissatisfied respondents cite insufficient attention rather than only quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Social and cultural issues (abortion, race relations, gun rights, LGBT rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover social and cultural issues like abortion, race relations, gun rights and LGBT rights (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the lowest-rated topic areas (32% excellent/good); often seen as politicized and subject to partisan disagreement; dissatisfaction split between amount and quality depending on party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Drug addiction
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do local news organizations cover drug addiction (excellent/good/fair/poor)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority say coverage is fair/poor and many cite insufficient attention (65% indicate not enough attention) rather than just poor quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount vs. quality as reasons for dissatisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: When respondents rate coverage 'fair' or 'poor', do they believe it's because the topic isn't given enough attention or because it's covered poorly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to interpret roots of dissatisfaction: e.g., drug addiction, environment, education wounds more because of insufficient attention; politics, weather, sports, crime more because of quality concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give information you can use in your daily life
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you generally have more trust in local news organizations or national ones to give information you can use in your daily life?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of eight trust facets where local news strongly outperforms national (79% local vs. 19% national). Important for perceived utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report the news without bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you generally have more trust in local news organizations or national ones to report the news without bias?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key dimension: 66% trust local more than national. Perception of bias strongly correlates with overall trust and partisan differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly identify editorials, commentaries or advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you generally have more trust in local or national news to clearly identify editorials, commentaries or advertisements to distinguish these from news reporting?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as a transparency indicator; local more trusted than national by a majority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on different ways that problems can be solved
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you generally have more trust in local or national news to report on different ways that problems can be solved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses constructive/journalistic breadth; local typically favored but partisan and attention-level differences exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get the facts right (accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you generally have more trust in local or national news to get the facts right?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical trust indicator; local is trusted more overall but Democrats more likely to trust national on accuracy. Strong driver of overall trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give adequate attention to all sides of an issue (balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you generally have more trust in local or national news to give adequate attention to all sides of an issue?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance is a major component of trust; local news is generally favored except on presentation/production quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give enough attention to the most important issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you generally have more trust in local or national news to give enough attention to the most important issues?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures agenda-setting relevance; local news often favored for daily-use topics, Democrats sometimes favor national here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present high-quality, professional broadcasts, newspapers or websites (professional presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you generally have more trust in local or national news to present high-quality, professional broadcasts, newspapers or websites?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the one dimension where national news often outperforms local; identifies resource/production gaps in many local outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived ideological leaning of local news relative to respondent
rubrics_metrics.description: How do respondents characterize the political leanings of news organizations in their local area compared with themselves (much more liberal to much more conservative)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure partisan alignment; those perceiving local media much more liberal than they are (15%) reduce trust. Differences in perceived ideology explain part of partisan trust gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptions of change in local news ideology over five years
rubrics_metrics.description: Compared to five years ago, has coverage from news organizations in your local area moved in a more liberal direction, more conservative direction, or stayed about the same?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 51% say 'stayed about the same', 37% 'more liberal', 11% 'more conservative'. Perceiving a change is associated with substantially lower trust (31% vs 55%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived mix of local vs. nonlocal stories (current and preferred percentage)
rubrics_metrics.description: What percentage of coverage by news organizations in your area is about things happening in your local area vs. outside, and what percentage would you prefer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mean perceived local share = 59%, mean preferred = 63%; 87% prefer at least half local. Limits how much local outlets can substitute nonlocal/national stories without alienating audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local vs national trust gap driver (distrust of national media)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the local–national trust gap driven by high trust in local news or by distrust in national media?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report concludes the gap is driven largely by distrust of national media among Republicans and independents rather than high enthusiasm for local news. Important when diagnosing strategies to increase trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence in local news relative to other local institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: How much confidence do you have in local libraries, law enforcement, churches, businesses, schools, courts, news organizations, and local government?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local news ranks low compared with most local institutions (37% high confidence), only local government ranks lower. Used to contextualize trust levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience community attachment and attention to local news as predictors
rubrics_metrics.description: Are respondents strongly attached to their community or follow local news closely, and how does that relate to their ratings of local news coverage?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong attachment and high attention correlate with substantially higher ratings (e.g., 67% of those who follow the news a great deal rate local govt/politics coverage excellent/good vs. 24% of those who don't). Useful for segmentation and outreach strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists' perceived attributes (caring, trustworthy, accurate, neutral) relative to national journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Do Americans view local journalists as more caring, trustworthy, accurate, and neutral/unbiased than national journalists?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported percentages: local journalists more likely to be seen as caring (36% vs. 4% national), trustworthy (29% vs. 8%), accurate (25% vs. 8%), neutral/unbiased (23% vs. 10%). Republicans especially favor local journalists on these attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental finding: labeling effect vs partisan bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental evidence: respondents rate the same news story as more trustworthy when identified as from a local organization vs national, unless the article's partisan leaning is obvious (partisan cues overwhelm local labeling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a contextual trust advantage for local labeling that can be negated by perceived partisan slant; implications for branding and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic and partisan differences in trust
rubrics_metrics.description: How do trust and evaluations vary by political affiliation, age, race/ethnicity, and other demographics?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant partisan gaps (Democrats more trusting overall; Republicans much more distrustful of national media). Older people and those more attentive to news are generally more trusting; African Americans have slightly higher trust in local news than whites/Hispanics but less trust in many other institutions.
